title: Nepal confers honorary rank of General on Indian Army chief - ThePrint
description: Nepal confers honorary rank of General on Indian Army chief  ThePrint
publisher.title: ThePrint
full_article:
The tradition began in 1950, when then Indian Army Chief Gen K M Cariappa was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepal Army. It emerged in the context of the India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, signed in July 1950, which provided the broader framework for closer ties between the two countries.

Nepal’s decision was reciprocated later that year, when the then Nepal Army Chief Gen Sir Kiran Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana was made an Honorary General of the Indian Army. The practice has continued since then, with the serving Army Chiefs of the two countries being given the honorary rank of General by the other country.

The appointment does not give the recipient any command or authority over another country’s army. It is a ceremonial military distinction, intended to underline the unusually close relationship between the two armies.

The military relationship itself is considerably older. Gorkha soldiers have served in the Indian Army for more than two centuries now. Recruitment and deployment of Nepali Gorkha soldiers have continued under an arrangement between India, Nepal and the UK since independence.

However, this has been stopped after India introduced the Agnipath scheme. Meanwhile, the Indian Army in a statement said that more than a ceremonial honour, the reciprocal conferment is an institutional expression of mutual trust, professional respect and military camaraderie between the two Armies.

Sustained across successive generations of military leadership, the ceremony therefore represents both tradition and strategic continuity. It underscores the commitment towards the steadfast nature of India-Nepal Military ties.

Nepal shares a border of over 1,850 km with five Indian states – Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

नेपाल केरऽ ई फैसला के प्रतिफल वू साल के बाद मिललै, जब॑ तत्कालीन नेपाली सेना प्रमुख जनरल सर किरण शुमशेर जंग बहादुर राना क॑ भारतीय सेना केरऽ मानद जनरल बनालऽ गेलै । तहिया सँ ई प्रथा जारी अछि, दुनू देशक सेवारत सेना प्रमुख केँ दोसर देश द्वारा जनरल केर मानद पद देल गेल अछि ।

नियुक्ति सं प्राप्तकर्ता कें दोसर देश कें सेना पर कोनों कमान या अधिकार नहि देल जायत छै. ई एगो विधिवत सैन्य भेद छै, जेकरऽ उद्देश्य दूनू सेना के बीच असामान्य रूप स॑ घनिष्ठ संबंध क॑ रेखांकित करना छै ।

सैन्य संबंध स्वयं काफी पुरान अछि। गोरखा जवान भारतीय सेना मे आब दू शताब्दी स बेसी स सेवारत छथि। आजादी के बाद स भारत, नेपाल आ ब्रिटेन के बीच भेल व्यवस्था के तहत नेपाली गोरखा सैनिक के भर्ती आ तैनाती जारी अछि।

मुदा भारत द्वारा अग्निपथ योजना शुरू करलाक बाद एकरा रोकल गेल अछि। एम्हर भारतीय सेना नँ एक बयान जारी क कहलकै कि ई पारस्परिक सम्मान स॑ बेसी ई पारस्परिक सम्मान दूनू सेना के बीच आपसी विश्वास, पेशेवर सम्मान आरू सैन्य साथी के संस्थागत अभिव्यक्ति छै ।

सैन्य नेतृत्व केरऽ लगातार पीढ़ी भर म॑ बनलऽ ई समारोह ई लेली परंपरा आरू सामरिक निरंतरता दूनू के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै । ई भारत-नेपाल सैन्य संबंध के स्थिर प्रकृति के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता के रेखांकित करै छै ।

नेपाल केरऽ सीमा भारत केरऽ पाँच राज्यऽ – सिक्किम, पश्चिम बंगाल, बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश आरू उत्तराखंड के साथ १,८५० किलोमीटर स॑ भी अधिक के सीमा छै ।

title: Durgalal Shrestha, poet who championed Nepal Bhasha literature, dies at 93 - The Kathmandu Post
description: Durgalal Shrestha, poet who championed Nepal Bhasha literature, dies at 93  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Poet and lyricist Durgalal Shrestha, one of the best-known poets of modern Nepal Bhasha literature, died at his home in Budhanilkantha on Sunday night. He was 93.



Kishan Sundar Malla, chancellor of the Nepal Bhasha Academy and a close associate of Shrestha, said the poet’s death was a major loss to Nepal Bhasha literature. “He was born to write,” said Malla, describing Shrestha as a son of Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of learning.

Born in Nhyakatol in central Kathmandu in Nepal Sambat 1057, Shrestha was the son of Aashamoti and Ganesh Lal. He entered the literary world by writing plays, and in Nepal Sambat 1075, his poem ‘Santwana’ was published in Dharmodaya magazine. He later became best known as a poet, although he was also a lyricist, playwright and translator. In 2003, the Nepal Bhasha Parishad conferred Shrestha with the title of Janakavi—people’s poet.

Shrestha often recalled with pride that he wrote, directed and acted in a play in Nepal Bhasha when he was only 11. Street theatre was common in Kathmandu neighbourhoods at the time, and the experience began his long literary career.

Although he wrote poems, songs, plays, essays and translations, Shrestha became best known as a poet. His writing earned him the title Janakabi, or people’s poet, because his language was accessible to ordinary readers while carrying strong emotions and ideas.

Essayist Ramesh Kaji Sthapit, who followed Shrestha’s literary career closely, said the most striking quality of his poetry was its musicality. “His poems were like songs,” said Sthapit. Almost all could be sung because they had rhythm and melody.

Shrestha’s first book, ‘Chiniyamha Kisicha’, was a collection of children’s poems and became one of the best-selling books published in Nepal Bhasha. He went on to publish more than a dozen collections of poems and songs. His writing often dealt with nationalism, language and community advancement.

The veteran poet and lyricist also wrote in Nepali. His song ‘Phoolko Aankhama Phoolai Sansar’ remains among his best-known works.

Sthapit said Shrestha’s work as a playwright was often overshadowed by his poetry and songs. “His pen perhaps ran even faster for plays than for poems,” he said. “His plays were equally strong, but his identity as a poet and lyricist covered them.”

For Shrestha, literature was also a form of cultural activism. After Radio Nepal stopped broadcasting news in Nepal Bhasha in 1965, he became an active participant in the movement against the state’s one-language policy. Literary conferences were organised across Kathmandu Valley neighbourhoods for about a year against the policy, and Shrestha actively took part in them. His poems and songs from that period became part of the wider campaign for recognition of Nepal Bhasha.

Shrestha remained active in organisations devoted to Nepal Bhasha and Newari cultural rights, and became a founding member of Nepal Bhasa Manka Khala.

Shrestha’s influence extended beyond books. His neat handwriting became so closely associated with him that a type font was later named after him. His poems and songs have travelled beyond Nepal through translations.

Shresha’s funeral is scheduled for Tuesday; colleagues, admirers and members of the Nepal Bhasha community are expected to gather to pay their final respects. His body will be kept at the Nepal Bhasha Manka Khala building in Bijeshwari before a funeral procession and cremation at Karnadeep.

For a literary community that saw him as both a creator and an advocate, Shrestha’s death marks the end of an unusually long career—one that began with a child’s neighbourhood play and grew into a lifelong effort to make language, literature and identity speak to ordinary people.

आधुनिक नेपाल भाषा साहित्यक सुप्रसिद्ध कवि मे सँ एक कवि आ गीतकार दुर्गलाल श्रेष्ठक रविदिन राति बुधनिलकण्ठ स्थित अपन घर पर निधन भ गेलनि । हुनकर उम्र 93 साल छल।



नेपाल भाषा अकादमी के कुलपति आ श्रेष्ठ के घनिष्ठ सहयोगी किशन सुन्दर मल्ल कवि के मृत्यु नेपाल भाषा साहित्य के लेल एकटा पैघ नुकसान रहल बतौलनि । मल्ल श्रेष्ठ के हिन्दू विद्या के देवी सरस्वती के पुत्र बताबैत कहलकै, “लिखै के लेलऽ जन्मलऽ छेलै ।

नेपाल सम्बत १०५७ मे मध्य काठमाण्डौ के न्याकटोल मे जन्मल श्रेष्ठ आशमोती आ गणेश लाल के पुत्र छल । नाटक लिखि साहित्य जगत मे प्रवेश केलनि, आ नेपाल सम्बत 1075 मे हुनक कविता ‘संतवाना’ धर्मोदय पत्रिका मे प्रकाशित भेल छल | बाद मे कवि के रूप मे बेसी जानल-मानल भेलाह, यद्यपि ओ गीतकार, नाटककार आ अनुवादक सेहो छलाह । 2003 मे नेपाल भाषा परिषद् श्रेष्ठ केँ जनकवि—जनकविक ​​उपाधि सँ सम्मानित केलक।

श्रेष्ठ प्रायः गर्व सँ स्मरण करैत छलाह जे ओ नेपाल भाषा मे एकटा नाटक लिखने, निर्देशित आ अभिनय केने छलाह जखन ओ मात्र 11 वर्षक छलाह |ओहि समय मे काठमांडू मोहल्ला मे स्ट्रीट थिएटर आम बात छल, आ एहि अनुभव सँ हुनक दीर्घ साहित्यिक जीवनक शुरुआत भेलनि ।

यद्यपि ओ कविता, गीत, नाटक, निबंध आ अनुवाद लिखैत छलाह, मुदा श्रेष्ठ कविक रूप मे बेसी जानल-मानल भेलीह । हुनकऽ लेखन के कारण हुनका जनकबी या जन कवि के उपाधि मिललै, कैन्हेंकि हुनकऽ भाषा प्रबल भाव आरू विचार के साथ-साथ आम पाठकऽ लेली सुलभ छेलै ।

श्रेष्ठ के साहित्यिक जीवन के बारीकी स॑ अनुसरण करै वाला निबंधकार रमेश काजी स्थापित न॑ कहलकै कि हुनकऽ कविता के सबसें हड़ताली गुण ओकरऽ संगीतमय छै । स्थपित कहलनि जे, हुनकर कविता गीत जकाँ छल। लगभग सबटा गाओल जा सकैत छल कारण एहि मे लय आ राग छल ।

श्रेष्ठक पहिल पोथी ‘चिनियामहा किसिचा’ बाल कविता संग्रह छल आ नेपाल भाषा मे प्रकाशित बेस्ट सेलिंग पोथी मे सँ एक बनल । आगू बढ़ि दर्जन भरि सँ बेसी कविता आ गीत संग्रह प्रकाशित केलनि । हिनक लेखन मे प्रायः राष्ट्रवाद, भाषा आ सामुदायिक उन्नतिक विषय छल ।

दिग्गज कवि आ गीतकार नेपाली मे सेहो लिखलनि । हिनक गीत ‘फुलको आंखामा फूलै संसार’ हिनक सर्वप्रसिद्ध रचना मे बनल अछि ।

स्थपित कहलनि जे श्रेष्ठक नाटककारक रूप मे काज पर प्रायः हुनक कविता आ गीतक छाया पड़ैत छलनि । ओ कहलनि जे, हुनकर कलम शायद कविता स बेसी तेजी स नाटक लेल चलैत छल। “हुनकर नाटक सेहो ओतबे मजबूत छल, मुदा कवि आ गीतकारक रूप मे हुनकर पहिचान ओकरा झाँपि देने छल।”

श्रेष्ठ के लेलऽ साहित्य भी सांस्कृतिक सक्रियता के एक रूप छेलै । 1965 मे रेडियो नेपाल नेपाल भाषा मे समाचार प्रसारण बंद केलाक बाद राज्यक एक भाषा नीतिक विरुद्ध आन्दोलन मे सक्रिय सहभागी बनि गेलाह । नीति के विरुद्ध लगभग एक साल तक काठमांडू उपत्यका के मोहल्ला भर में साहित्यिक सम्मेलन के आयोजन करलऽ गेलै, आरू श्रेष्ठ सक्रिय रूप सें ओकरा में भाग लेलकै । ओहि कालखंडक हुनक कविता आ गीत नेपाल भाषाक मान्यताक व्यापक अभियानक अंग बनि गेल ।

श्रेष्ठ नेपाल भाषा आ नेवारी सांस्कृतिक अधिकार के प्रति समर्पित संस्था में सक्रिय रहल, आ नेपाल भासा मनका खाला के संस्थापक सदस्य बनल ।

श्रेष्ठ’क प्रभाव पोथी सँ आगू बढ़ि गेल छल. हुनकऽ सुव्यवस्थित हस्तलेख हुनका स॑ एतना घनिष्ठ रूप स॑ जुड़लऽ छेलै कि बाद म॑ हुनकऽ नाम प॑ एक टाइप फॉन्ट के नामकरण करलऽ गेलै । हिनक कविता आ गीत अनुवादक माध्यमे नेपालसँ बाहरक यात्रा कएने अछि ।

श्रेष्ठ’क अंतिम संस्कार मंगल दिन होबय बला अछि; सहयोगी, प्रशंसक आ नेपाल भाषा समुदाय के सदस्य सब के अंतिम श्रद्धांजलि देबय लेल एकत्रित हेबाक उम्मीद अछि। हुनकऽ शव क॑ कर्णदीप म॑ अंतिम संस्कार आरू अंतिम संस्कार स॑ पहल॑ बीजेश्वरी केरऽ नेपाल भाषा मनका खाला भवन म॑ रखलऽ जैतै ।

जे साहित्यिक समुदाय हुनका रचनाकार आरू पैरवीकार दोनों के रूप म॑ देखै छेलै, ओकरा लेली श्रेष्ठ केरऽ निधन एगो असामान्य रूप स॑ लम्बा कैरियर के अंत छेकै-जे एक बच्चा केरऽ पड़ोसी नाटक स॑ शुरू होय क॑ भाषा, साहित्य आरू पहचान क॑ आम लोगऽ स॑ बोलै के आजीवन प्रयास म॑ बदली गेलै ।

title: Finance Ministry delays forwarding MCA Nepal’s request to extend MCC projects - The Kathmandu Post
description: Finance Ministry delays forwarding MCA Nepal’s request to extend MCC projects  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
The Ministry of Finance has held up a request from the Millennium Challenge Account Nepal (MCA-Nepal) for a one-year extension of US-funded infrastructure projects, with the proposal yet to reach the US government’s Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC).

MCA-Nepal sent the request to the ministry mid-May, asking it to formally approach MCC headquarters for an extension of the $747 million projects, which include a 315-km transmission line and road upgrade works.

A senior finance ministry official told the Post that they had received a letter on behalf of MCA-Nepal but had not yet been forwarded to MCC headquarters. “It is still under discussion,” the official told the Post, without disclosing why the request had been held up or when it would be sent.

The MCA-Nepal board member said MCA-Nepal sent the request to the Finance Ministry, which serves as the liaison ministry and must formally approach the MCC headquarters on Nepal’s behalf. The finance secretary heads the MCA-Nepal board.

Under the MCC Compact, the projects are supposed to be completed by August 30, 2028. But MCA-Nepal says implementation has been delayed by about 14 months because of the US government’s temporary suspension of MCC operations and the cancellation and re-tendering of contracts for the transmission line.

“Due to some reasons, we have already sought a one-year term extension for the completion of the two projects,” said a senior MCA-Nepal board member who is not authorised to speak to the media.

“It has been three months since MCA-Nepal sent such a request to the finance ministry, but there is no information about the term extension,” the board member said.

Once the finance ministry forwards the request, the MCC headquarters will review the reasons cited by MCA-Nepal and decide whether to grant the extension.

In its letter, MCA-Nepal stated that due to some unavoidable circumstances, including US President Donald Trump’s decision in July 2025 to pause US foreign assistance and halt MCC payments. The suspension put the projects in limbo for several months before the administration decided in July 2025 to allow MCC’s global operations, including in Nepal, to continue.

MCA-Nepal also cited the cancellation of bids in October 2023 for construction of the 315-km 400kV transmission line after all bidders quoted prices substantially above the estimated cost.

Following the cancellation, MCA-Nepal had to restart the bidding process. It took almost nine months to award a fresh contract, an MCA-Nepal official told the Post.

The official said MCC headquarters is positive about the term extension and that a new US law could also facilitate the extension.

“First, the MCC headquarters itself is positive because our reasons are grounded and valid. Second, the Trump administration has introduced a new law that permits a one-year term extension to the projects currently in operation in four countries,” the official said.

MCA-Nepal is a government agency set up to manage the MCC Compact in Nepal.

The five-year compact was signed between the government of Nepal and MCC in September 2017. The US initially committed $500 million in grants, while Nepal agreed to contribute $150 million, which was later jacked up to $197 million. The total investment in two projects has therefore reached $697 million. The MCC board had also agreed to provide an additional $50 million to cover a funding gap, potentially taking the total value of the compact to $747 million.

Dragged into controversy, the compact was ratified by the House of Representatives in February 2022 and entered into force on August 30, 2023.

MCA-Nepal is seeking more time mainly because of delays in getting the projects off the ground. But officials say implementation continues to face problems, especially in the transmission line project.

The road project is progressing smoothly, they said. But the transmission line project has been held up by problems with land acquisition, compensation, construction quality and compliance with environmental rules.

Construction of substations has also raised quality concerns. Many people have yet to receive compensation for their land acquired for the transmission line’s right of way, according to officials. “So far compensation has been distributed for only 18 km of the transmission line’s right of way,” an official told the Post, adding, “How can contractors start work until they get the site clearance?”

“Land acquisition is still facing hurdles and has not been resolved despite a large team and resources being mobilised on the ground,” an official who regularly monitors the MCC projects from both the centre and the field.

“The way compensation is being provided to affected families and land owners under the MCC project could create problems for future transmission line projects. We may not be able to afford similar levels of compensation in other projects,” the official said.

Mahendranagar. Buddhiraj Chaudhary, a resident of Pachui in Belauri Municipality-8, Kanchanpur, has been living here for more than five decades. He is not satisfied as officials of the Indian Border Security Force have started obstructing the graveling of a 1,400-meter road in the Pachui village of the Dokebazar-Daiji Hulaki road section.

In February 2073 BS, the 64-kilometer Hulaki road from Dokebazar to Daiji in Bedkot Municipality was contracted in three packages. In Pachui, which falls in the middle package (second package), Indian security personnel have been obstructing construction, claiming the section falls on the Nepal-India border at the no-man's-land.

"Border pillar number 38 of Nepal-India falls in that area," said Chaudhary. "We have been considering the Sutiya River as the border for a long time. We also have about 20 bighas of sugarcane cultivation beyond the Hulaki section and this side of the Sutiya River."

Although Nepalis have been cultivating sugarcane this side of the Sutiya River, the Hulaki road section is this side of it (towards Nepal). Although Nepalis have been cultivating sugarcane for a long time without any problems, the Indian side has been obstructing the construction of the road, claiming it falls in the no-man's-land since the construction of the Hulaki road began, according to Mukund Prasad Lamiachhane, chief of the Hulaki Highway Project Office, Dhangadhi.

"We are preparing to re-tender the second package due to the negligence of the construction entrepreneur," he said. "In that same section, due to India's border disputes, including in the no-man's-land, the 1,400-meter section in the Pachui area could not be blacktopped. Now, the plan is to proceed with the work by leaving that part."

Local levels and local administration have been trying to resolve the dispute that has arisen in that area. However, a conclusion has not yet been reached, said Chief Lamiachhane.

Man Bahadur Chaudhary, a local of Pachui, said that the Indian side has been unnecessarily obstructing the construction of the Hulaki road, which falls on Nepali land for centuries.

"Since the blacktopping of the Hulaki road began, the area has been tightened, and Indian security personnel have not even allowed gravel to be laid to fill potholes," he said. He stated that diplomatic efforts from the higher level are necessary for blacktopping in that section.

Although the first and third packages of the Hulaki road have been constructed, the second package has not been built even after nine years due to the negligence of the construction company.

title: USU Moab Students Examine Healthcare Practices in Nepal Study Abroad Experience - Utah State University
description: USU Moab Students Examine Healthcare Practices in Nepal Study Abroad Experience  Utah State University
publisher.title: Utah State University
full_article:
MOAB, Utah — A group of Utah State University students traveled to Nepal as part of a two-week study abroad immersive learning experience centered around the local healthcare practices.

The trip of nine USU students included five from USU Moab. Students who participated in the program expanded their understanding of global health by navigating unfamiliar healthcare settings and embracing new ways of learning.

The students traveled to three different communities, giving service and collaborating with local healthcare workers at hospitals, clinics and community organizations. The students also gifted 10 water filtration systems to families in need.

The Moab campus partnered with the Utah nonprofit Youthlinc and Waves for Water, as well as the Nepal organization Insight Himalaya.

“Hospitals and schools were selected to give students experiences in public, private, rural, urban and specialty healthcare settings,” said Shanda Thompson, USU Moab academic advisor. “Study abroad can be a grounding experience for students and the direction they want to go once they finish their program. Our program was focused on healthcare, and it allowed students to see similarities and differences between our healthcare system and Nepal’s.”

Some of the local healthcare facilities the students saw included a maternity hospital. Nursing student Haley Rice, who is an aspiring NICU nurse, was amazed to see how the nurses at the hospital worked to meet the needs of patients while being equipped with scarce resources She said it reminded her that the heart of nursing is the people behind it.

“As a nursing student, this experience reminded me why I chose this career,” she said. “It made me want to be the kind of nurse who is compassionate, open-minded and willing to learn from people with different backgrounds and experiences. I came home with a new appreciation for the healthcare system we have, but also with a better understanding that there's always something we can learn from others.”

The trip also included a visit to a hospital that treated people with leprosy. The students were inspired by the resilience of patients and doctors and nurses alike in a setting that did not include basic amenities that the students took for granted, including air conditioning and clean drinking water.

“This experience made me realize how different healthcare can be in other parts of the world,” said nursing student Jeferlita Zul. “To actually see with your own eyes makes a huge difference. Seeing it firsthand made me appreciate what I have and gave me a new perspective on how lucky I am.”

In addition to their work, students saw remote regions of the mountains and hiked one of the most famous mountainous regions of the world.

“The trekking was definitely challenging, and at times it felt like we might have overdone it, but it was still an amazing experience,” Zul said. “I loved seeing the mountains and getting to visit places that felt very different from home. I still shed tears when people ask me about Nepal.”

Students described their experience as eye-opening.

“More than anything, Nepal taught me gratitude,” Rice said. “I came home with a greater appreciation for the opportunities I've had, the education I'm receiving, and the healthcare resources we often take for granted. The people we met were so welcoming, resilient and kind, and I know those are lessons I'll carry with me for the rest of my life, both as a person and someday as a nurse.”

More information is available at studyabroad.usu.edu or by contacting a USU Study Abroad advisor at studyabroad@usu.edu

काठमाडौं ।

Ncell has partnered with Cimex Inc, the authorised distributor of BYD Auto Industry Co. Ltd, in Nepal to deliver connected vehicle services powered by Ncell Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity.

The collaboration strengthens Ncell’s position at the forefront of IoT innovation in Nepal, building on its early adoption and growing portfolio of IoT solutions. Through this partnership, Ncell continues to drive the adoption of connected technologies across sectors.

With this, BYD customers in Nepal will now be able to enjoy a more seamless and digitally connected driving experience.

With this, compatible BYD vehicles delivered through BYD Nepal will now come equipped with an embedded Ncell IoT SIM. This enables direct in-vehicle internet connectivity that supports the BYD App ecosystem and connected infotainment features. ई सहयोग स॑ नेपाल म॑ आईओटी नवाचार म॑ एनसेल केरऽ स्थिति मजबूत होय जाय छै, जे ओकरऽ जल्दी अपनाबै आरू आईओटी समाधान केरऽ बढ़तऽ पोर्टफोलियो के आधार प॑ होय छै । अइ साझेदारी कें माध्यम सं एनसेल क्षेत्रक मे जुडल तकनीक कें अपनानाय कें बढ़ावा देनाय जारी रखयत छै.

एहि स नेपाल मे बीवाईडी क ग्राहक आब बेसी निर्बाध आ डिजिटल रूप स जुड़ल ड्राइविंग अनुभव क आनंद ल सकैत छथि।

एकरऽ साथ ही बीवाईडी नेपाल के माध्यम स॑ डिलीवर करलऽ जाय वाला संगत बीवाईडी वाहन अब॑ एम्बेडेड एनसेल आईओटी सिम स॑ लैस आबै वाला छै । इ सीधा वाहन मे इंटरनेट कनेक्टिविटी कें सक्षम बनायत छै जे बीवाईडी ऐप इकोसिस्टम आ कनेक्टेड इन्फोटेनमेंट सुविधाक कें समर्थन करयत छै. उपयोगकर्ता सीधा वाहन कें सिस्टम कें माध्यम सं यूट्यूब, स्पोटिफाई, कराओके आ अन्य डिजिटल मनोरंजन जैना ऑनलाइन सेवाक कें उपयोग कयर सकय छै, बिना कोनों फोन कनेक्ट करय कें जरूरत कें या वाई-फाई हॉटस्पॉट पर भरोसा करय कें.

व्यक्तिगत सुविधाक उपलब्धता नेपाल मे उपलब्ध वाहन मॉडल, सॉफ्टवेयर संस्करण आ सेवा पर निर्भर करैत अछि । कनेक्टिविटी एनसेल कें मजबूत मोबाइल नेटवर्क पर काज करयत छै आ उपयोगकर्ता कें अनुभव कवरेज, स्थान आ वाहन विन्यास कें आधार पर भिन्न भ सकय छै ठीक ओना जेना एनसेल सिम कें उपयोग करयत छै.

एहि साझेदारी स सिर्फ नव कार मालिक कए नहि बल्कि पहिने स बीवाईडी वाहन क मालिक कए सेहो फायदा होएत। ओ अपन वर्तमान वाहन मे एनसेल आईओटी सिम प्राप्त करय आ समर्थित कनेक्टेड फीचर तक पहुंचय लेल नेपाल मे 13 स्थान पर पसरल नामित बीवाईडी अधिकृत सेवा केंद्र नेटवर्क पर जा सकैत छथि.

After repeated demands by opposition lawmakers, Speaker Aryal directed Prime Minister Shah to respond to questions raised in the House concerning matters under his jurisdiction, according to sources in the Parliament secretariat.

In his maiden appearance in the parliament on May 31, Shah had said that he has learnt about his country “encroaching” territories in India.

Later, the Foreign Ministry said PM Shah’s comments were related to “no-man’s land encroachments” and “cross-border occupation” between the two countries, rather than any territorial claims.

Opposition lawmakers said the prime minister should either provide evidence to support his claim that Nepal had encroached on Indian territory or withdraw the statement.

title: Army chief Gen Seth’s Nepal visit carries strategic weight - MillenniumPost
description: Army chief Gen Seth’s Nepal visit carries strategic weight  MillenniumPost
publisher.title: MillenniumPost
full_article:
New Delhi: Chief of Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth’s three-day visit to neighbouring Nepal, which started on Monday, is particularly timely in the context of Indian-Nepalese relations, with much more significance than the routine and formal elements of military diplomacy usually involve.

In view of the ongoing change in the strategic equation of the Himalayan subcontinent, Seth’s visit provides an excellent chance for New Delhi to consolidate one of the most lasting security relationships that it has.

While ostensibly focused on deepening defence cooperation between the two countries, General Seth’s trip will undoubtedly open up the possibility for talks covering topics like border security, intelligence sharing, military training, disaster management and institutional cooperation. But underneath all these aspects of defence cooperation lies a more serious concern of how India and Nepal can sustain their longstanding military relationship against the backdrop of a fast-changing security environment in the region.

Experts feel that the Gorkha connection continues to be at the centre of this relationship. For many years now, the recruitment of Nepalese nationals in the Indian Army has acted as a special link between the two nations, forging not just military ties but also strong socio-institutional links. Now, given the unresolved issue of the recruitment of Nepali Gorkhas through the Agnipath scheme, this aspect has become an important part of the larger picture of the defence relationship. Thus, the visit by Gen Seth acquires special importance in this context.

In terms of the geopolitical environment, the engagement becomes even more significant. Nepal’s efforts to carefully tread on the delicate issue of maintaining a balanced relationship with India and China have started gaining strategic importance for India.

The traditional practice of conferring the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army on the Indian Army chief adds another layer of symbolism to the visit, as it symbolises the trust and respect developed by the two militaries over the years and is a unique aspect of their defence relations. Hence, during the first day of his visit, General Seth, was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army by Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel in Kathmandu, which is rooted in a longstanding military tradition, symbolises mutual trust, professional camaraderie and the enduring strategic partnership between India and Nepal.

However, more importantly, the meeting of General Seth is occurring at a time when India is making efforts to enhance its relations with Nepal’s political, diplomatic, and military establishments. In this way, the visit of the Indian Army Chief could be a significant vehicle for strategic communication.

In the case of New Delhi, the overriding goal is obvious: ensuring that the long-standing military cooperation between India and Nepal is still relevant to the security issues of the 21st century.

हिमालय उपमहाद्वीप केरऽ सामरिक समीकरण म॑ जारी बदलाव क॑ देखत॑ हुअ॑ सेठ केरऽ ई यात्रा नई दिल्ली लेली एगो बेहतरीन मौका प्रदान करै छै कि वू सबसें स्थायी सुरक्षा संबंधऽ म॑ स॑ एक क॑ मजबूत करी सक॑ ।

जहाँ कथित तौर प॑ दूनू देशऽ के बीच रक्षा सहयोग क॑ गहरा करै प॑ केंद्रित छै, वहीं जनरल सेठ केरऽ ई यात्रा स॑ निस्संदेह सीमा सुरक्षा, खुफिया जानकारी साझा करै, सैन्य प्रशिक्षण, आपदा प्रबंधन आरू संस्थागत सहयोग जैसनऽ विषय प॑ बातचीत के संभावना खुलतै । लेकिन रक्षा सहयोग केरऽ ई सब पहलू के नीचे ई बात के आरू गंभीर चिंता छै कि ई क्षेत्र म॑ तेजी स॑ बदलत॑ सुरक्षा वातावरण के पृष्ठभूमि म॑ भारत आरू नेपाल अपनऽ लंबा समय स॑ चलै वाला सैन्य संबंध क॑ कोना कायम रखै सकै छै ।

विशेषज्ञ सब के लगैत छनि जे गोरखा कनेक्शन एहि संबंध के केंद्र में बनल रहैत अछि. आब कतेको वर्ष सँ भारतीय सेना मे नेपाली नागरिकक बहाली दुनू राष्ट्रक बीच एकटा विशेष कड़ीक काज करैत रहल अछि, जाहि सँ मात्र सैन्य संबंध नहि अपितु मजबूत सामाजिक-संस्थागत संबंध सेहो बनल अछि । आब अग्निपथ योजना के माध्यम स नेपाली गोरखा के भर्ती के अनसुलझल मुद्दा के देखैत ई पहलू रक्षा संबंध के पैघ तस्वीर के एकटा महत्वपूर्ण अंग बनि गेल अछि। एहि तरहें जनरल सेठक यात्रा एहि संदर्भ मे विशेष महत्व प्राप्त करैत अछि ।

भू-राजनीतिक परिवेशक दृष्टिएँ ई जुड़ाव आओर बेसी महत्वपूर्ण भ' जाइत अछि । भारत आरू चीन के साथ संतुलित संबंध बनाबै के नाजुक मुद्दा प॑ सावधानी स॑ कदम रखै के नेपाल केरऽ प्रयास क॑ भारत लेली सामरिक महत्व मिलना शुरू होय गेलऽ छै ।

भारतीय सेना प्रमुख क॑ नेपाली सेना केरऽ जनरल केरऽ मानद पद प्रदान करै के पारंपरिक प्रथा ई यात्रा म॑ प्रतीकात्मकता के एगो आरू परत जोड़ै छै, कैन्हेंकि ई दूनू सेना द्वारा वर्षो स॑ विकसित विश्वास आरू सम्मान के प्रतीक छै आरू ओकरऽ रक्षा संबंध केरऽ एगो अनूठा पहलू छै । अतः अपनऽ यात्रा केरऽ पहिलऽ दिन जनरल सेठ क॑ काठमांडू म॑ नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रपति रामचंद्र पौडेल न॑ नेपाली सेना केरऽ जनरल के मानद पद स॑ सम्मानित करलकै, जे दीर्घकालीन सैन्य परंपरा म॑ जड़ जमाय क॑ आपसी विश्वास, पेशेवर साथी आरू भारत आरू नेपाल के बीच स्थायी सामरिक साझेदारी के प्रतीक छै ।

लेकिन, एकरा स॑ भी महत्वपूर्ण बात ई छै कि जनरल सेठ केरऽ ई मुलाकात ऐन्हऽ समय म॑ होय रहलऽ छै जब॑ भारत नेपाल केरऽ राजनीतिक, कूटनीतिक, आरू सैन्य प्रतिष्ठानऽ स॑ अपनऽ संबंध बढ़ाबै के प्रयास करी रहलऽ छै । एहि तरहें भारतीय सेना प्रमुखक यात्रा सामरिक संचारक लेल एकटा महत्वपूर्ण साधन बनि सकैत अछि ।

नई दिल्ली के मामला म॑ एकरऽ प्रमुख लक्ष्य स्पष्ट छै कि भारत आरू नेपाल के बीच लंबा समय स॑ चलै वाला सैन्य सहयोग अखनी भी 21वीं सदी के सुरक्षा मुद्दा के साथ प्रासंगिक छै ।

full_article:
APO-backed plans handed over to governments for implementation.

Asian Productivity Organisation (APO) member economies Cambodia and Nepal have received new roadmaps from APO in support of their national development. Both Cambodia and Nepal are looking to change their status from the "least developed country" designation.

Cambodia's government, which received its APO-backed National Productivity Master Plan in 2018, was recently handed the Institutional Capability Development Plan (ICDP) for the National Productivity Centre of Cambodia (NPCC).

Through 10 reform actions and a three-year capability pathway, the ICDP seeks to improve service effectiveness, stakeholder engagement, and results-based management whilst strengthening institutional and governance foundations as well as organisational systems and human capabilities.

APO Secretary-General Dr. Indra Pradana Singawinata (pictured left), referring to the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology, and Innovation (MISTI), commented: "The true value of this development plan will depend on implementation.

"With sustained leadership from MISTI, strong ownership by the NPCC, adequate human and financial resources, effective partnerships, and disciplined monitoring of progress, the NPCC can further strengthen its role as Cambodia's national productivity institution and make a deeper contribution to the country's long-term competitiveness, innovation, and prosperity."

The ICDP was received by H.E. Hem Vanndy (pictured right), MISTI Minister, during an official handover ceremony in Phnom Penh.

The event in Cambodia took place eight days after the Nepalese government received its own APO-supported productivity roadmap, which is the National Productivity Master Plan for Nepal 2026–2036.

The 10-year master plan for Nepal is based on targets to improve the business-enabling environment in the country, accelerate innovation-led modernisation, build competitiveness and economic complexity, and increase productivity through climate resilience and inclusion.

The APO Secretary-General noted: "Nepal has an opportunity to demonstrate that productivity is not merely a technocratic exercise but a national pathway to stronger competitiveness, greater economic resilience, and shared prosperity.

"By translating this master plan into concrete action, Nepal can build a more productive, innovative, and inclusive future for generations to come.

Krishna Bahadur Raut (APO Director for Nepal and Secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies) expressed full commitment in institutionalising the recommendations set out in the productivity plan.

"The Ministry, alongside the NPEDC (National Productivity and Economic Development Centre), will spearhead the coordination, cross-governmental collaboration, and monitoring mechanisms required to bring these strategic thrusts to life," he said.

Aimed at increasing productivity in Asia Pacific, the APO was established in 1961 as an intergovernmental organisation. Its other member economies include Bangladesh, China, Fiji, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Turkiye, and Vietnam.

एशियाई उत्पादकता संगठन (एपीओ) के सदस्य अर्थव्यवस्था कम्बोडिया आरू नेपाल क॑ अपनऽ राष्ट्रीय विकास के समर्थन म॑ एपीओ स॑ नया रोडमैप मिललऽ छै । कम्बोडिया आरू नेपाल दोनों देश "कम विकसित देश" पदनाम स॑ अपनऽ दर्जा बदलै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छै ।

10 सुधार कार्यवाही आ तीन साल कें क्षमता मार्ग कें माध्यम सं आईसीडीपी सेवा प्रभावशीलता, हितधारक कें जुड़ाव, आ परिणाम आधारित प्रबंधन मे सुधार करय कें कोशिश करय छै आ संस्थागत आ शासन नींव कें संग-संग संगठनात्मक प्रणाली आ मानव क्षमता कें मजबूत करय कें कोशिश करय छै.

एपीओ केरऽ महासचिव डॉ. इंद्र प्रदान सिंगाविनाता (चित्र बायां) न॑ उद्योग, विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी, आरू नवाचार मंत्रालय (एमआईएसटीआई) के जिक्र करतें हुअ॑ टिप्पणी करलकै कि ई विकास योजना केरऽ असली मूल्य कार्यान्वयन प॑ निर्भर करतै ।

एशिया प्रशांत म॑ उत्पादकता बढ़ाबै के उद्देश्य स॑ एपीओ केरऽ स्थापना १९६१ म॑ एगो अंतरसरकारी संगठन के रूप म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । एकरऽ अन्य सदस्य अर्थव्यवस्था म॑ बांग्लादेश, चीन, फिजी, हांगकांग, भारत, इंडोनेशिया, ईरान, जापान, लाओस, मलेशिया, मंगोलिया, पाकिस्तान, फिलीपींस, सिंगापुर, दक्षिण कोरिया, श्रीलंका, थाईलैंड, तुर्की, आरू वियतनाम शामिल छै ।

title: Indonesia, India, and Nepal Collaborate to Explore Beneficial Insect Biodiversity for Food Security and a Green Economy in Asia - ANTARA News Sumbar
description: Indonesia, India, and Nepal Collaborate to Explore Beneficial Insect Biodiversity for Food Security and a Green Economy in Asia  ANTARA News Sumbar
publisher.title: ANTARA News Sumbar
full_article:
Padang (ANTARA) - Indonesia, India, and Nepal are strengthening an international research collaboration to study the biodiversity of beneficial insects as an important asset for food security and the development of sustainable green-economy agriculture in Asia. Through the International Research Network, or IRN, Universitas Andalas is collaborating with Punjabi University in India and Tribhuvan University in Nepal to develop research that views insects not merely as small components of ecosystems, but as essential organisms supporting pollination, ecological cycles, agricultural productivity, and community economic opportunities.

The international collaboration involves Prof. Dr. Henny Herwina from Universitas Andalas, Prof. Dr. Himender Bharti from the Department of Zoology and Environmental Sciences, Punjabi University, India, and Dr. Indra Prasad Subedi from the Central Department of Zoology, Tribhuvan University, Nepal. The partnership with these two universities has continued throughout the 2025–2026 research period. This study serves as an initial step toward understanding the position and importance of beneficial insects within tropical Asian landscapes. The current phase of field research focuses on different land-use systems in Sumatra, while the research network with India and Nepal strengthens the scientific perspective and creates opportunities for broader studies of insect biodiversity across Asia in the future.

Another form of this collaboration was demonstrated through the participation of Prof. Dr. Himender Bharti as one of the invited speakers in a Summer Course organized by the Department of Biology, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, Universitas Andalas, from May 25 to June 12, 2026. The program was conducted through both online and offline activities under the main theme “Integrated Tropical Forest Biodiversity Assessment.” It involved participants from eight countries, including researchers and students from Nepal.



The main insect groups receiving attention in this research collaboration include Coleoptera, or beetles, Lepidoptera, which comprises butterflies and moths, and Hymenoptera, particularly bees and ants. Odonata, including dragonflies and damselflies, is also observed as an important component of the insect community. The study does not merely record the presence of these insects. It also seeks to understand how different land-use systems influence insect diversity and how these groups can be sustainably utilized as beneficial insects.

From Forests to Farms, Insects Reveal the Condition of the Environment

Sampling was conducted across different land-use landscapes in Sumatra. The habitats observed were highly diverse, ranging from forests, mangosteen orchards, rubber plantations, mixed-crop farms, and maize fields to fragmented forests around university campuses.

These contrasting landscapes are important from an ecological perspective. A forest with multiple layers of vegetation naturally provides a different living environment from a monoculture farming system dominated by a single crop. The availability of flowering plants, nesting trees, organic matter, leaf litter, dead wood, and the overall structure of vegetation can determine which insects are able to survive and establish their populations.

Lepidoptera emerged as a prominent group in terms of species richness, while Hymenoptera dominated in terms of the number of individuals recorded. The high number of butterfly and moth species reflects considerable species richness, whereas the abundance of Hymenoptera indicates a strong presence of social insects, particularly ants and bees.

Lepidoptera represents one of the most conspicuous insect groups identified in the study. Butterflies offer ecological value far beyond the beauty and colors of their wings. Their presence is closely associated with vegetation quality and habitat conditions. For this reason, Lepidoptera diversity can provide important information about the ability of a landscape to sustain insect communities amid continuing changes in land use.

In addition to butterflies, Coleoptera, or beetles, constitutes another important group examined in this research. Their presence is associated with complex habitat structures, including decomposing organic materials, dead wood, and diverse vegetation that provide suitable habitats for different beetle groups.

Beetles perform a broad spectrum of ecological functions. Within an ecosystem, various Coleoptera species are involved in decomposition processes, food webs, and the utilization of organic materials. Understanding beetle communities therefore also means understanding part of the ecological processes that quietly operate on forest floors and within agricultural landscapes.



This research offers a different perspective on insects. Not all insects should be regarded as agricultural pests. Many species work almost invisibly, maintaining ecological processes that ultimately contribute to the sustainability of agricultural systems.

Bees Are Small in Size, but Enormous in Value

Hymenoptera shows a different ecological pattern. While Lepidoptera is prominent in terms of species richness, Hymenoptera dominates in individual abundance. The high abundance of this group reflects the strong presence of social insects such as ants and bees within the research landscapes.

The value of bees extends even further into community-based economic opportunities. Besides providing essential pollination services, stingless bees and honey bees produce economically valuable commodities such as honey, bee pollen, propolis, and various other bee products. The research identifies these pollinator groups as potentially important assets for supporting sustainable green-economy agriculture in Asia.



Research Does Not Stop in the Laboratory

One of the most interesting aspects of this program is the effort to bring scientific knowledge beyond academic laboratories and directly into communities. Knowledge about beneficial insects has been translated into practical training activities for local people.

Community members were introduced to the cultivation of galo-galo, the local term for stingless bees, along with colony management, safe honey-harvesting techniques, and post-harvest processing. These activities are intended to provide livelihood alternatives that are relatively environmentally friendly while simultaneously encouraging pollinator conservation.

Galo-galo honey can subsequently be developed into value-added products, including honey-based confectionery. At this point, the meaning of beneficial insects becomes very tangible. A bee may be physically small, but the network of benefits surrounding it can extend to agricultural crops, ecosystem health, and household incomes.

The potential use of honey bees for agriculture and human well-being is also promising, including opportunities for ecotourism and bee-related therapeutic activities.

Toward an Asian Beneficial Insect Biodiversity Network

The collaboration among Universitas Andalas, Punjabi University, and Tribhuvan University provides a foundation for broader research on beneficial insects across Asia. Indonesia possesses exceptionally rich tropical ecosystems, India covers an extensive and diverse biogeographical landscape, while Nepal presents distinctive ecological gradients ranging from lowlands to mountainous regions.

The integration of scientific expertise from these three countries has the potential to enrich our understanding of the relationships among biodiversity, land-use change, and agricultural sustainability.



Ultimately, this research carries a simple but important message. Butterflies, beetles, and bees are not merely secondary inhabitants of agricultural landscapes. They are part of the ecological machinery that keeps natural systems functioning.

When insect biodiversity is conserved, what is being protected is not merely the number of species. Pollination processes, habitat health, agricultural productivity, and economic opportunities for communities are also maintained.

From Sumatra, through scientific collaboration among researchers from Indonesia, India, and Nepal, this research seeks to place these small organisms in a more appropriate position within Asia’s broader development agenda, recognizing them as strategic biological assets for food security, sustainable agriculture, and the future of the green economy.

This activity was funded by the Indonesian Endowment Fund for Education (LPDP) on behalf of the Indonesian Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Technology, and managed under the EQUITY Program, Contract No. 4304/B3/DT.03.08/2025.

पड़ंग (अंतरा) - इंडोनेशिया, भारत, आरू नेपाल न॑ खाद्य सुरक्षा आरू एशिया म॑ टिकाऊ हरित अर्थव्यवस्था वाला कृषि के विकास लेली एगो महत्वपूर्ण संपत्ति के रूप म॑ फायदेमंद कीड़ा-मकोड़ा के जैव विविधता के अध्ययन लेली एगो अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शोध सहयोग क॑ मजबूत करी रहलऽ छै । इंटरनेशनल रिसर्च नेटवर्क या आईआरएन के माध्यम स॑ यूनिवर्सिटास अंडलास भारत केरऽ पंजाबी विश्वविद्यालय आरू नेपाल केरऽ त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय के साथ मिल क॑ ऐन्हऽ शोध विकसित करी रहलऽ छै जे कीड़ा-मकोड़ा क॑ खाली पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र केरऽ छोटऽ घटक के रूप म॑ नै, बल्कि परागण, पारिस्थितिकी चक्र, कृषि उत्पादकता, आरू सामुदायिक आर्थिक अवसरऽ के समर्थन करै वाला आवश्यक जीव के रूप म॑ देखै छै ।

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सहयोगमे युनिवर्सिटास अण्डलाससँ प्रो. ई दूनू विश्वविद्यालयऽ के साथ साझेदारी पूरा २०२५-२०२६ के शोध अवधि म॑ जारी छै । ई अध्ययन उष्णकटिबंधीय एशियाई परिदृश्य के भीतर लाभकारी कीड़ा-मकोड़ा के स्थिति आरू महत्व क॑ समझै के दिशा म॑ एगो प्रारंभिक कदम के रूप म॑ काम करै छै । क्षेत्रीय अनुसंधान केरऽ वर्तमान चरण सुमात्रा केरऽ विभिन्न भूमि उपयोग प्रणाली प॑ केंद्रित छै, जबकि भारत आरू नेपाल के साथ शोध नेटवर्क वैज्ञानिक परिप्रेक्ष्य क॑ मजबूत करै छै आरू भविष्य म॑ पूरा एशिया म॑ कीट जैव विविधता के व्यापक अध्ययन के अवसर पैदा करै छै ।

ई सहयोग केरऽ एगो आरू रूप के प्रदर्शन जीव विज्ञान विभाग, गणित आरू प्राकृतिक विज्ञान संकाय, यूनिवर्सिटास अंडलास द्वारा 25 मई स॑ 12 जून, 2026 तलक आयोजित एगो समर कोर्स म॑ आमंत्रित वक्ता के रूप म॑ प्रो जैव विविधता आकलन।” एहि मे नेपालक शोधकर्ता आ छात्र सहित आठ देशक प्रतिभागी शामिल छलाह ।



ई शोध सहयोग म॑ ध्यान देलऽ जाय वाला मुख्य कीट समूहऽ म॑ कोलिओप्टेरा या भृंग, लेपिडोप्टेरा, जेकरा म॑ तितली आरू पतंग शामिल छै, आरू हाइमेनोप्टेरा, खास करी क॑ मधुमक्खी आरू चींटी शामिल छै । ड्रैगनफली आरू डैमसेल्फली सहित ओडोनाटा भी कीड़ा समुदाय केरऽ एगो महत्वपूर्ण घटक के रूप म॑ देखलऽ जाय छै । अध्ययन म॑ खाली ई कीड़ा-मकोड़ा केरऽ उपस्थिति के रिकॉर्डिंग नै करलऽ गेलऽ छै । इ इ समझय कें सेहो कोशिश करय छै की विभिन्न भूमि-उपयोग प्रणाली कीड़ा-मकोड़ा कें विविधता कें कोना प्रभावित करय छै आ इ समूहक कें लाभकारी कीड़ाक कें रूप मे कोना टिकाऊ उपयोग कैल जा सकय छै.

जंगल स खेत तक कीड़ा-मकोड़ा पर्यावरण के हालत के उजागर करैत अछि |

सुमात्रा केरऽ विभिन्न भूमि उपयोग परिदृश्यऽ म॑ नमूना लेलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । देखलऽ गेलऽ आवास बहुत विविध छेलै, जेकरा म॑ जंगल, आम के बगीचा, रबर के बागान, मिश्रित फसल के खेत, आरू मक्का के खेत स॑ ल॑ क॑ विश्वविद्यालय परिसरऽ के आसपास के खंडित जंगल तक छेलै ।

पारिस्थितिकी के दृष्टिकोण स॑ ई विपरीत परिदृश्य महत्वपूर्ण छै । वनस्पति कें अनेक परत वाला जंगल स्वाभाविक रूप सं एकल फसल कें प्रधानता वाला एकल खेती प्रणाली सं अलग रहय कें वातावरण प्रदान करयत छै. फूलक पौधा, घोंसला बनाबय वाला गाछ, जैविक पदार्थ, पात कें कूड़ा, मृत लकड़ी, आ वनस्पति कें समग्र संरचना कें उपलब्धता इ निर्धारित कयर सकय छै की कोन कीड़ा जीवित रहय मे सक्षम छै आ ओकर आबादी स्थापित करय मे सक्षम छै.

प्रजाति समृद्धि के मामला म॑ लेपिडोप्टेरा एगो प्रमुख समूह के रूप म॑ उभरलै, जबकि रिकॉर्ड करलऽ गेलऽ व्यक्ति के संख्या के मामला म॑ हाइमेनोप्टेरा के बोलबाला छेलै । तितली आरू पतंग केरऽ प्रजाति केरऽ अधिक संख्या काफी प्रजाति समृद्धि क॑ दर्शाबै छै, जबकि हाइमेनोप्टेरा केरऽ प्रचुरता सामाजिक कीड़ा-मकोड़ा, खास करी क॑ चींटी आरू मधुमक्खी केरऽ मजबूत उपस्थिति के संकेत दै छै ।

लेपिडोप्टेरा अध्ययन म॑ पहचानलऽ गेलऽ सबसें स्पष्ट कीड़ा समूहऽ म॑ स॑ एक के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै । तितली अपनऽ पाँखऽ के सुंदरता आरू रंग स॑ बहुत आगू पारिस्थितिकी मूल्य प्रदान करै छै । एकरऽ उपस्थिति वनस्पति केरऽ गुणवत्ता आरू आवास केरऽ स्थिति स॑ गहराई स॑ जुड़लऽ छै । अइ कारण सं लेपिडोप्टेरा विविधता भूमि उपयोग मे लगातार बदलाव कें बीच कीड़ा समुदायक कें बनाए रखय कें लेल कोनों परिदृश्य कें क्षमता कें बारे मे महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी प्रदान कयर सकय छै.

तितली के अलावा कोलिओप्टेरा या भृंग एकटा आरू महत्वपूर्ण समूह के गठन करै छै जेकरऽ जांच ई शोध म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छै । एकरऽ उपस्थिति जटिल आवास संरचना स॑ जुड़लऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ विघटित जैविक सामग्री, मृत लकड़ी, आरू विविध वनस्पति शामिल छै जे विभिन्न भृंग समूहऽ लेली उपयुक्त आवास प्रदान करै छै ।

भृंग पारिस्थितिकी कार्यक कें एकटा व्यापक स्पेक्ट्रम करएयत छै. एक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र के भीतर, विभिन्न कोलिओप्टेरा प्रजाति अपघटन प्रक्रिया, खाद्य जाल, आरू जैविक सामग्री के उपयोग म॑ शामिल होय छै । अइ कें लेल भृंग समुदायक कें समझय कें मतलब पारिस्थितिकी प्रक्रियाक कें हिस्सा कें समझनाय सेहो छै जे वन कें तल पर आ कृषि परिदृश्यक कें भीतर चुपचाप संचालित होयत छै.



ई शोध कीड़ा-मकोड़ा के बारे म॑ एगो अलग नजरिया पेश करै छै । सब कीड़ा-मकोड़ा कें कृषि कीट नहि मानल जेबाक चाही. बहुत प्रजाति लगभग अदृश्य रूप सं काज करएयत छै, पारिस्थितिकी प्रक्रियाक कें बनाए रखएयत छै जे अंततः कृषि प्रणालीक कें स्थायित्व मे योगदान करएयत छै.

मधुमाछी आकार मे छोट होइत अछि, मुदा मूल्य मे विशाल होइत अछि

हाइमेनोप्टेरा एकटा अलग पारिस्थितिकी पैटर्न देखबैत अछि । जहाँ लेपिडोप्टेरा प्रजाति समृद्धि के दृष्टि स॑ प्रमुख छै, वहीं हाइमेनोप्टेरा व्यक्तिगत प्रचुरता म॑ हावी छै । ई समूह केरऽ उच्च प्रचुरता शोध परिदृश्य के भीतर चींटी आरू मधुमक्खी जैसनऽ सामाजिक कीड़ा-मकोड़ा केरऽ मजबूत उपस्थिति क॑ दर्शाबै छै ।

मधुमक्खी कें मूल्य समुदाय आधारित आर्थिक अवसरक मे आ बेसि विस्तारित छै. आवश्यक परागण सेवा प्रदान करय कें अलावा डंक रहित मधुमक्खी आ मधुमक्खी आर्थिक रूप सं मूल्यवान वस्तुअक जेना शहद, मधुमक्खी कें पराग, प्रोपोलिस, आ विभिन्न अन्य मधुमक्खी उत्पादक कें उत्पादन करय छै. शोध इ परागणक समूहक कें एशिया मे टिकाऊ हरित अर्थव्यवस्था कृषि कें समर्थन कें लेल संभावित रूप सं महत्वपूर्ण संपत्ति कें रूप मे पहचान करय छै.



प्रयोगशाला मे शोध नहि रुकैत अछि

ई कार्यक्रम केरऽ एगो सबसें रोचक पहलू छै वैज्ञानिक ज्ञान क॑ शैक्षणिक प्रयोगशाला स॑ परे आरू सीधे समुदाय म॑ लानै के प्रयास । लाभकारी कीड़ा-मकोड़ा कें बारे मे ज्ञान कें स्थानीय लोगक कें लेल व्यावहारिक प्रशिक्षण गतिविधियक मे बदलल गेल छै.

समुदाय के सदस्यऽ क॑ कॉलोनी प्रबंधन, सुरक्षित शहद-कटाई के तकनीक, आरू फसल के बाद के प्रसंस्करण के साथ-साथ डंक रहित मधुमक्खी के लेलऽ स्थानीय शब्द गैलो-गालो के खेती स॑ परिचित कराय देलऽ गेलै । इ गतिविधियक कें उद्देश्य आजीविका विकल्प उपलब्ध करानाय छै जे अपेक्षाकृत पर्यावरण कें अनुकूल होयत छै आ संगे-संग परागणक संरक्षण कें प्रोत्साहित करनाय छै.

एकरऽ बाद गैलो-गालो शहद क॑ मूल्य वर्धित उत्पाद म॑ विकसित करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै, जेकरा म॑ शहद आधारित हलवाई भी शामिल छै । एतय लाभकारी कीड़ा-मकोड़ाक अर्थ बहुत मूर्त भ' जाइत अछि । मधुमक्खी शारीरिक रूप सं छोट भ सकय छै, मुदा ओकरा आसपास कें लाभक कें जाल कृषि फसलक, पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र कें स्वास्थ्य, आ घरक कें आय तइक पहुंच सकय छै.

कृषि आरू मानव कल्याण लेली मधुमक्खी के संभावित उपयोग भी आशाजनक छै, जेकरा म॑ इकोटूरिज्म आरू मधुमक्खी स॑ जुड़लऽ चिकित्सीय गतिविधियऽ के अवसर भी शामिल छै ।

एक एशियाई लाभकारी कीट जैव विविधता नेटवर्क की ओर |

यूनिवर्सिटास अंडलास, पंजाबी विश्वविद्यालय, आरू त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय के बीच के सहयोग स॑ पूरा एशिया म॑ फायदेमंद कीड़ा-मकोड़ा प॑ व्यापक शोध के आधार मिलै छै । इंडोनेशिया के पास असाधारण रूप स॑ समृद्ध उष्णकटिबंधीय पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र छै, भारत म॑ विस्तृत आरू विविध जैव भौगोलिक परिदृश्य छै, जबकि नेपाल निचला भूमि स॑ ल॑ क॑ पहाड़ी क्षेत्र तलक के विशिष्ट पारिस्थितिकी ढाल प्रस्तुत करै छै ।

इ तीनू देशक सं वैज्ञानिक विशेषज्ञता कें एकीकरण सं जैव विविधता, भूमि उपयोग परिवर्तन, आ कृषि स्थायित्व कें बीच संबंधक कें बारे मे हमर समझ कें समृद्ध करय कें क्षमता छै.



अंततः ई शोध एकटा सरल मुदा महत्वपूर्ण संदेश दैत अछि । तितली, भृंग, आ मधुमाछी केवल कृषि परिदृश्यक गौण निवासी नहि छै. ई पारिस्थितिकी मशीनरी के हिस्सा छै जे प्राकृतिक प्रणाली क॑ काम करतें रखै छै ।

जखन कीड़ा-मकोड़ाक जैव विविधता कें संरक्षण कैल जायत छै तखन जे सुरक्षा कैल जा रहल छै, ओ केवल प्रजातियक कें संख्या नहि छै. परागण प्रक्रिया, आवास स्वास्थ्य, कृषि उत्पादकता, आ समुदायक कें लेल आर्थिक अवसरक कें सेहो कायम राखल जायत छै.

सुमात्रा स॑ ल॑ क॑ इंडोनेशिया, भारत आरू नेपाल केरऽ शोधकर्ता सिनी के बीच वैज्ञानिक सहयोग के माध्यम स॑ ई शोध ई छोटऽ जीवऽ क॑ एशिया केरऽ व्यापक विकास एजेंडा के भीतर अधिक उपयुक्त स्थिति म॑ रखै के कोशिश करै छै, जेकरा म॑ एकरा खाद्य सुरक्षा, टिकाऊ कृषि, आरू हरित अर्थव्यवस्था के भविष्य लेली रणनीतिक जैविक संपत्ति के रूप म॑ पहचानलऽ जाय छै ।

इ गतिविधि कें वित्तपोषण इंडोनेशियाई उच्च शिक्षा, विज्ञान, आ प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय कें तरफ सं इंडोनेशियाई एण्डोवमेंट फंड फॉर एजुकेशन (एलपीडीपी) द्ववारा कैल गेलय छेलै, आ इक्विटी कार्यक्रम, अनुबंध संख्या 4304/बी3/डीटी.03.08/2025 कें तहत प्रबंधित कैल गेलय छेलै.

title: TB treatment is free in Nepal, but 51 percent of affected families face crippling costs: Report - The Kathmandu Post
description: TB treatment is free in Nepal, but 51 percent of affected families face crippling costs: Report  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Laxmi Chaudhary from Dhangadhi Sub-metropolitan City in Kailali district has been living in Kathmandu for the past one year for treatment of gland TB, medically known as tuberculous lymphadenitis.

The 54-year-old was referred to Bir Hospital by doctors at Seti Provincial Hospital in Dhangadhi after her condition did not improve even after a year of medication.

“In the initial stage, she used to come to Kathmandu every month,” said Dr Prajowl Shrestha, senior chest physician and associate professor at the National Academy of Medical Sciences. “But when she ran out of money, she decided to rent a room in Kathmandu. Expenses were huge, as she had to bring her family members also.”

Although tuberculosis medicines are provided free of charge in Nepal, a new study shows that 51 percent of households with a TB patient face catastrophic costs due to the disease.

According to a report titled ‘Catastrophic Costs and Impoverishment Among Tuberculosis-Affected Households in Nepal: Results from a National Patient Cost Survey,’ free medicines and clinical services alone are not enough to protect TB-affected families from financial hardship.

These costs include spending on medical tests, transportation, food and accommodation, as well income lost due to illness.

“One in two TB-affected households in Nepal face catastrophic costs despite free diagnosis and treatment,” the report published recently in Health Policy and Planning, a peer-reviewed international scientific journal published by Oxford University Press, stated. “Drug-resistant TB leaves three in four affected households facing catastrophic costs in Nepal.”

Tuberculosis, or TB, is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which most commonly affects the lungs. When people with pulmonary TB cough, sneeze, or spit, they release TB bacteria into the air, and people who inhale them can become infected.

Along with medicines, the government provides sputum testing and chest x-rays free of charge for TB diagnosis, but patients must pay out of pocket for other investigations, including CT scans, MRI scans, and some laboratory tests, which can be costly.

“Some TB patients also have to undergo cerebrospinal fluid analysis, tissue biopsies and pleural fluid tests,” said Dr Shrestha, who is a principal investigator of the study. “These and other tests do not come under the free scheme.”

Besides the lungs, TB can affect other parts of the body, including the lymph nodes, bones and joints, brain, kidneys, urinary tract, abdomen, intestines, liver, spleen, reproductive organs, skin and eyes, and multiple tests are required to diagnose the ailments, Shrestha said.

The study, which included 1,000 patients enrolled in the National Tuberculosis Programme, found that the financial burden was primarily driven by direct non-medical costs, which accounted for 44 percent of the total costs.

Direct medical costs included out-of-pocket payments for consultations, laboratory tests, and medications. Direct nonmedical costs comprised expenditures for transportation, food, accommodation, and nutritional supplements or additional food.

Indirect costs, mainly income lost due to illness and treatment, accounted for another 39 percent. Indirect costs represented the economic value of time lost due to illness and care-seeking and were estimated using the human-capital approach.

Total costs for the entire TB episode were estimated by aggregating three components: pretreatment costs, intensive-phase costs, and continuation-phase costs, according to the report.

Of the total participants, over one-third (36 percent) were the primary income earner in their households.

“TB-related costs pushed 13 percent of households below the poverty line, increasing to 31 percent among DR-TB households,” reads the report.

Overall, 35 percent of participants reported borrowing money to cover treatment-related expenses, including 42percent of those with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) and 31 percent of those with drug-susceptible TB (DS-TB).

A smaller proportion had to sell assets such as land, livestock or gold jewellery to meet these expenses—5.7 percent of DS-TB patients and 7.7 percent of DR-TB patients.

Nepal continues to face a substantial TB burden. According to the latest WHO estimates, around 67,000 people developed TB in Nepal in 2024, equivalent to an incidence rate of 227 cases per 100,000 population. TB also caused an estimated 16,000 deaths in the country that year— 44 people every day.

Of the estimated 67,000 people who developed TB in 2024, only 38,606 were diagnosed and received treatment, leaving a substantial number of people with the disease undetected and untreated. Health officials say these missing cases pose a serious challenge to controlling the further spread of TB.

“Finding hidden cases in communities is the main challenge for us in controlling tuberculosis,” said Dr Bhuwan Paudel, director of the National Tuberculosis Control Centre. “Despite various efforts, we have not been able to detect all the estimated TB patients.”

Nepal has committed to ending TB through the WHO End TB Strategy by 2035. But the National Prevalence Survey carried out in 2018-19 with the technical and financial support from the WHO showed that the country is “not on track’ to meet the target.

The survey estimated that 117,000 people were living with TB at the time.

Nepal started providing TB treatment some 93 years ago, but it continues to remain one of the major public health burdens.

Dr Shrestha said Chaudhary needs extended treatment, which could last several months, and he must remain under close supervision by medical personnel.

“I have already spent all I could in my treatment,” Shrestha quoted Chaudhary as complaining. “Now, there is no one in my village to provide additional loans either.”

कैलाली जिल्लाके धनगढी उपमहानगरपालिकाके लक्ष्मी चौधरी विगत एक वर्षसे काठमाण्डौमे ग्रन्थ टीबी, चिकित्सकीय रूपसे क्षयरोगी लिम्फडेनाइटिसके नामसे जानल जाएके उपचारके लेल रहि रहल अछि ।

धनगढीके सेती प्रादेशिक अस्पतालमे ५४ वर्षीय महिलाके एक वर्ष दवाई खलाके बादो अवस्थामे सुधार नै भेलाबाद डाक्टरसब बीर अस्पताल रेफर केने छल ।

नेशनल एकेडमी ऑफ मेडिकल साइंसेज के वरिष्ठ छाती चिकित्सक आ एसोसिएट प्रोफेसर डॉ. प्रजौल श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, प्रारंभिक अवस्था मे ओ हर महीना काठमांडू अबैत छलीह। “मुदा पाइ खतम भेला पर काठमांडू मे एकटा कोठली किराया पर लेबाक निर्णय लेलनि, खर्चा बहुत पैघ छल, कारण परिवारक लोक केँ सेहो आनय पड़ैत छलनि।”

नेपाल मे क्षय रोगक दवाई निःशुल्क उपलब्ध कराओल जाइत अछि, मुदा एकटा नव अध्ययन सँ पता चलल अछि जे टीबी रोगी वाला ५१ प्रतिशत घर मे एहि बीमारी के कारण विनाशकारी खर्च के सामना करय पड़ैत अछि ।

‘नेपाल मे क्षयरोग सं प्रभावित घरक मे आपदाजनक लागत आ दरिद्रता: राष्ट्रीय रोगी लागत सर्वेक्षण कें परिणाम’ शीर्षक कें रिपोर्ट कें अनुसार टीबी प्रभावित परिवारक कें आर्थिक कष्ट सं बचाव कें लेल केवल मुफ्त दवाई आ नैदानिक ​​सेवाक पर्याप्त नहि छै.

एहि लागत मे मेडिकल टेस्ट, परिवहन, भोजन आ आवास पर खर्च के संग-संग बीमारी के कारण नुकसान के आमदनी सेहो शामिल अछि.

ऑक्सफोर्ड यूनिवर्सिटी प्रेस द्वारा प्रकाशित सहकर्मी द्वारा समीक्षित अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वैज्ञानिक पत्रिका हेल्थ पॉलिसी एंड प्लानिंग मे हाल मे प्रकाशित रिपोर्ट मे कहल गेल अछि जे, नेपाल मे टीबी प्रभावित दू मे स एक घर मे मुफ्त निदान आ इलाज क बावजूद विनाशकारी लागत क सामना करय पड़ैत अछि। “नशा प्रतिरोधी टीबी के कारण नेपाल मे चारि मे सँ तीन प्रभावित घर मे विनाशकारी लागत के सामना करय पड़ैत छैक।”

क्षय रोग या टीबी माइकोबैक्टीरियम ट्यूबरकुलोसिस के कारण होइत अछि जे बेसीतर फेफड़ा के प्रभावित करैत अछि । जखन फुफ्फुसीय टीबी कें रोगी खांसी, छींकएय या थूकएयत छै, तखन ओ टीबी कें बैक्टीरिया हवा मे छोड़एयत छै, आ जे लोग ओकरा सांस लेयत छै, ओकरा संक्रमित भ सकएय छै.

दवाई के साथ-साथ सरकार टीबी के निदान के लेल थूक के जांच आ छाती के एक्स-रे के सुविधा मुफ्त में दैत अछि, मुदा मरीज के जेब सं दोसर जांच के लेल पैसा देबय पड़त, जाहि में सीटी स्कैन, एमआरआई स्कैन, आ किछु प्रयोगशाला जांच शामिल अछि, जे महग भ सकैत अछि.

अध्ययन के प्रधान अन्वेषक डॉ. श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, किछु टीबी के मरीज के सेरेब्रोस्पाइनल फ्लूइड एनालिसिस, टिश्यू बायोप्सी आ फुफ्फुसीय फ्लूइड टेस्ट सेहो करय पड़ैत छनि। “ई आ अन्य टेस्ट मुफ्त योजना मे नहि अबैत अछि।”

फेफड़ा के अलावा टीबी शरीर के अन्य अंग, जेकरा म॑ लिम्फ नोड्स, हड्डी आरू जोड़, मस्तिष्क, गुर्दा, मूत्रमार्ग, पेट, आंत, यकृत, प्लीहा, प्रजनन अंग, त्वचा आरू आँख शामिल छै, प्रभावित होय सकै छै आरू बीमारी के निदान लेली कई तरह के जांच के जरूरत होय छै, श्रेष्ठ न॑ कहलकै ।

राष्ट्रीय क्षय रोग कार्यक्रम म॑ नामांकित १,००० मरीजऽ क॑ शामिल करलऽ गेलऽ ई अध्ययन म॑ पता चललै कि आर्थिक बोझ मुख्य रूप स॑ प्रत्यक्ष गैर-चिकित्सा लागत के कारण छै, जे कुल लागत के ४४ प्रतिशत छै ।

प्रत्यक्ष चिकित्सा लागत में परामर्श, प्रयोगशाला परीक्षण, आ दवाई के लेल जेब सं बाहर भुगतान शामिल छल. प्रत्यक्ष गैर-चिकित्सा लागत मे परिवहन, भोजन, आवास, आ पोषण पूरक या अतिरिक्त भोजन कें लेल खर्च शामिल छल.

अप्रत्यक्ष लागत, मुख्य रूप स बीमारी आ इलाज क कारण नुकसान भेल आय, आओर 39 प्रतिशत छल। अप्रत्यक्ष लागत बीमारी आरू देखभाल-खोज के कारण खो गेलऽ समय के आर्थिक मूल्य के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छेलै आरू मानव-पूंजी दृष्टिकोण के उपयोग करी क॑ एकरऽ अनुमान लगैलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, पूरा टीबी एपिसोड के लेल कुल लागत के अनुमान तीन घटक के एकत्रित क लेल गेल छल: पूर्व उपचार लागत, गहन-चरण लागत, आ निरंतरता-चरण लागत.

कुल प्रतिभागी मे सं एक तिहाई सं बेसि (36 प्रतिशत) अपन घर मे प्राथमिक आय अर्जित करय वाला छल.

रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि टीबी स॑ जुड़लऽ लागत न॑ १३ प्रतिशत घरऽ क॑ गरीबी रेखा स॑ नीचें धकेल॑ देलकै, जे डीआर-टीबी वाला घरऽ म॑ बढ़ी क॑ ३१ प्रतिशत होय गेलै ।

कुल मिलाकय, 35 प्रतिशत प्रतिभागियक कें रिपोर्ट छै कि ओ इलाज सं संबंधित खर्चक कें कवर करय कें लेल पैसा उधार लेने छै, जेकरा मे 42 प्रतिशत दवा प्रतिरोधी टीबी (डीआर-टीबी) आ 31 प्रतिशत दवा संवेदनशील टीबी (डीएस-टीबी) सं पीड़ित शामिल छै.

एकटा छोट हिस्सा कें एहि खर्च कें पूरा करय कें लेल जमीन, पशुधन या सोना कें गहना जैना संपत्ति बेचय कें छल-डीएस-टीबी कें 5.7 प्रतिशत रोगी आ 7.7 प्रतिशत डीआर-टीबी कें मरीज.

नेपालमे टीबीके पर्याप्त बोझ जारी अछि । डब्ल्यूएचओ केरऽ ताजा अनुमान के अनुसार २०२४ म॑ नेपाल म॑ लगभग ६७,००० लोगऽ म॑ टीबी केरऽ संक्रमण होय गेलऽ छेलै, जे प्रति एक लाख आबादी म॑ २२७ केस के घटना दर के बराबर छै । टीबी सं सेहो ओहि साल देश मे अनुमानित 16,000 लोकक मौत भेल छल- हर दिन 44 लोक.

2024 म॑ टीबी केरऽ शिकार होय वाला अनुमानित 67,000 लोगऽ म॑ स॑ केवल 38,606 लोगऽ के निदान होय ​​गेलै आरू ओकरऽ इलाज करलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ काफी संख्या म॑ ई बीमारी स॑ पीड़ित लोगऽ के पता नै चललै आरू ओकरऽ इलाज नै होय गेलै । स्वास्थ्य अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे ई लापता मामला टीबी के आओर फैलाव पर नियंत्रण के लेल गंभीर चुनौती अछि.

राष्ट्रीय क्षय नियंत्रण केंद्र के निदेशक डॉ. भुवन पौडेल कहलनि जे, समुदाय मे छिपल मामला के खोजनाय हमरा सब लेल क्षय रोग पर नियंत्रण मे मुख्य चुनौती अछि। “विभिन्न प्रयास के बावजूद हम सब अनुमानित टीबी के मरीज के पता नै लगा सकलौं।”

नेपाल 2035 तक डब्ल्यूएचओ एंड टीबी रणनीति के माध्यम सं टीबी के समाप्त करय के प्रतिबद्धता जतौने अछि.मुदा डब्ल्यूएचओ के तकनीकी आ आर्थिक सहयोग सं 2018-19 मे कएल गेल राष्ट्रीय प्रसार सर्वेक्षण मे पता चलल जे देश लक्ष्य के पूरा करय लेल “पटरी पर नहि” अछि.

सर्वेक्षण मे अनुमान लगाओल गेल अछि जे ओहि समय एक लाख 17 हजार लोक टीबी सं पीड़ित छलाह.

नेपाल टीबी के इलाज करीब 93 साल पहिने शुरू केने छल, मुदा एखनो ई जनस्वास्थ्य के प्रमुख बोझ मे सं एक बनल अछि.

डॉ. श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे चौधरी के विस्तारित इलाज के जरूरत अछि, जे कतेको महीना तक भ सकैत अछि, आ हुनका मेडिकल कर्मी के बारीकी सं देखरेख मे रहय पड़त।

श्रेष्ठ चौधरी के उद्धृत करैत कहलनि जे, हम अपन इलाज मे जतेक खर्च भ सकैत छल, ओतबे खर्च क चुकल छी। “आब, हमर गाम मे सेहो अतिरिक्त कर्ज देबय वाला कियो नहि अछि।”

title: PMO scrutiny of Nepal Telecom billing tender raises concerns over interference - The Kathmandu Post
description: PMO scrutiny of Nepal Telecom billing tender raises concerns over interference  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
The prime minister’s office (PMO) has begun examining the tender process and technical specifications for Nepal Telecom’s proposed new billing system, prompting concerns within the state-owned operator over what employees describe as growing external involvement in technical and procurement decisions.

The information technology section of the PMO instructed the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology on May 27 to provide documents related to the procurement, with a copy sent to Nepal Telecom. The requested records include procurement documents, system design and architecture diagrams, geographic information system frameworks and details of the company’s 4G/LTE operations.

The review is being conducted by an information technology study task force under the PMO, according to Hemraj Aryal, PMO spokesman.

“Our IT study task force is reviewing the issues related with the billing system,” Aryal told Kantipur. “However, a comprehensive report detailing specific findings has not yet been submitted. Detailed insights will be accessible once the task force concludes its evaluation.”

Aryal said the review was a routine assessment and was not intended to interfere with Nepal Telecom’s procurement or operations.

“It is merely a standard study intended to assess the overall status of public information technology infrastructure,” he said. “The task force was previously constituted to review various IT systems across state organs. This routine assessment is unlikely to halt or impede Nepal Telecom’s ongoing operational procedures.”

The explanation has done little to ease concerns among senior Nepal Telecom officials, who argue that decisions involving the company’s core systems should be guided by established technical and procurement processes rather than political or administrative intervention.

The scrutiny comes as Nepal Telecom prepares fresh tender documents for a new billing system estimated to cost around Rs5 billion. Previous attempts to procure the system were stalled by legal challenges, complaints over tender specifications and administrative decisions.

The company’s board has recently delegated full authority to the managing director to execute the procurement, apparently to streamline decision-making and prevent further delays.

Nepal Telecom joint spokesperson Prakschet Thapa Chhetri said preparations for the revised tender were under way.

“Our technical team is working intensively. Given the intricate and highly sensitive nature of this procurement, thorough preparation is mandatory,” he said. “Once finalised, the details will be released transparently into the public domain. We view the prime minister’s office’s interest as a constructive and supportive gesture.”

Dispute over splitting the system

The latest scrutiny followed a request from the IT study task force for historical and current records relating to Nepal Telecom’s billing and other systems. The company initially submitted digital copies of tender documents by email, but officials at Singha Durbar later asked telecom representatives to provide physical copies.

“The tender documents were already available publicly on the Public Procurement Monitoring Office website,” said an employee familiar with the process, speaking on condition of anonymity. “Yet, after being pressured by central officials, our staff spent hours photocopying thousands of pages of technical archives.”

The request has also revived an earlier debate over whether Nepal Telecom should procure the billing system as a single integrated platform or split it into separate contracts. According to telecom officials, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, reflecting views from the prime minister’s office, initially favoured separating the system’s software and hardware, with part of the software to be potentially developed by domestic companies.

Under the proposed model, Nepal Telecom would retain the Online Charging System (OCS) and hardware infrastructure, while the Business Support System (BSS) would be procured or developed separately.

The proposal met resistance from Nepal Telecom’s management and employee unions, who argued that the billing platform is not simply a commercial software application but a core telecommunications system closely linked to customer identities, SIM registration, international roaming and real-time usage information. Separating the integrated system, they said, could create gaps in responsibility during failures and increase security and operational risks.

“This infrastructure integrates international roaming protocols, real-time location tracking, and critical socio-economic indicators,” said Lokendra Paneru, general secretary of the Nepal Telecom Workers’ Union. “It handles live profiles and data streams involving everyone, from high-ranking government officials to ordinary citizens. Approaching it casually poses immense national risks.”

Telecom engineers have similarly argued that the OCS and BSS, while performing different functions, operate within an integrated architecture and require coordinated hardware, software and technical support.

Following technical briefings from Nepal Telecom, officials at the prime minister’s office have reportedly softened their earlier position.

A senior PMO official, speaking on condition of anonymity, acknowledged that separate procurement had previously been proposed.

“A joint proposal had previously been drafted by ministry leadership and prime minister’s advisers recommending the split procurement model,” the official said. “However, Nepal Telecom’s technical team maintained a firm stance that breaking up an integrated architecture creates severe accountability gaps during system failures.”

The dispute has thus moved beyond whether the government should scrutinise a major public procurement. It has raised a broader question over how far administrative oversight should extend into technical decisions at a state-owned telecommunications operator, particularly as delays could jeopardise the replacement of an ageing system.

Previous tenders faced legal hurdles

The current procurement is the latest attempt to replace Nepal Telecom’s ageing billing infrastructure, which was installed in 2011 by Chinese technology company AsiaInfo-Linkage Technologies. The system has remained in operation through successive contract extensions, with the current arrangement due to expire in 2027.

Efforts to replace it have been dogged by controversy and legal challenges. Earlier tender specifications were criticised for allegedly favouring Huawei Technologies, which already supplies significant network infrastructure to Nepal Telecom. Critics argued that awarding both network infrastructure and billing functions to the same vendor could deepen vendor lock-in and create risks involving competition, system dependence and data security.

The dispute eventually reached the Supreme Court, which directed Nepal Telecom to reduce its dependence on a single vendor and ensure adequate safeguards for privacy and data security.

Despite the ruling, subsequent technical evaluations again qualified Huawei while disqualifying other bidders, including Whale Cloud, renewing questions over whether the tender requirements allowed sufficient competition.

A Huawei Nepal representative defended the limited participation of international vendors, saying major global suppliers such as Ericsson, Oracle and CSG rarely participate in Nepal government tenders. That, the representative said, leaves a limited pool of vendors capable of meeting Nepal Telecom’s technical requirements.

The procurement also came under scrutiny from within the government. In November 2025, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology formed an investigation panel led by former secretary Mani Ram Gelal after complaints alleging manipulation of the tender process.

The panel’s report warned that rigid qualification criteria could favour particular bidders and raised concerns over outdated procurement arrangements and potential financial liabilities for the state-owned company. The findings added to questions over how Nepal Telecom should structure a procurement involving a system that is both technically complex and critical to its daily operations.

The billing division had previously faced scrutiny from the Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority. In May 2024, the anti-graft body filed corruption charges against former Nepal Telecom managing director Sunil Poudel and former chief business officer Sangeeta Pahadi Aryal over alleged irregularities in maintenance contracts. Pahadi Aryal was later cleared of the charges by the court and has since returned to an executive leadership role at Nepal Telecom.

Delays threaten transition

The prolonged procurement process has increased pressure on Nepal Telecom to replace its ageing system before the current contract expires.

Replacing a billing platform of this scale involves migrating large volumes of customer and network data, testing and integrating the new system, and running the old and new platforms in parallel. Nepal Telecom officials say a complex migration and data transfer requires at least 24 months of operational preparation.

Any further delay in awarding the contract could therefore leave less time for a controlled transition before the existing arrangement expires in 2027.

The concern is not only financial. A billing system processes subscriber information, usage records, account balances, charging and other functions essential to a telecommunications operator. Problems during migration could affect customers nationwide, disrupt revenue collection and compromise service management.

Nepal Telecom’s legacy infrastructure has already experienced periodic problems, with disruptions affecting mobile and data services. The Nepal Telecommunications Authority (NTA) has intervened following complaints and directed the operator to strengthen backup arrangements.

“The authority dispatched technical inspection teams to monitor network failures firsthand and directed Nepal Telecom to maintain backup systems,” said NTA spokesperson Min Prasad Aryal. “Our primary focus remains enforcing statutory quality-of-service mandates and compliance with license obligations.”

Nepal Telecom says the existing system has not caused an immediate financial loss, but continued reliance on ageing infrastructure could constrain its ability to expand services and handle growing traffic.

Joint spokesperson Thapa said previous attempts to launch a replacement tender had been stalled by administrative and legal challenges.

“We attempted to launch new tenders in the past, but administrative and legal challenges stalled progress, forcing us to make temporary fixes to the existing hardware,” he said. “If we fail to upgrade the core infrastructure systematically, network performance will deteriorate, directly impacting customer service efficiency across the country.”

The need for a replacement is also linked to Nepal Telecom’s plans to expand next-generation services, including 5G. A modern billing platform would be expected to handle more complex products, real-time charging and higher transaction volumes as data use grows.

For Nepal Telecom, the challenge is therefore to replace a system approaching the end of its extended contractual life without introducing new technological dependencies or operational vulnerabilities.

The prime minister’s office maintains that its involvement is limited to a technical review, while Nepal Telecom says it welcomes scrutiny and intends to conduct the procurement transparently.

अर्याल कहलनि जे ई समीक्षा नियमित आकलन अछि आ एकर उद्देश्य नेपाल दूरसंचारक खरीद वा परिचालन मे हस्तक्षेप नहि करबाक अछि।

हुनी कहलकै, 'ई महज एगो मानक अध्ययन छै जेकरौ उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी बुनियादी ढाँचा के समग्र स्थिति के आकलन करना छै । “पहिने राज्य के अंग मे विभिन्न आईटी प्रणाली के समीक्षा के लेल टास्क फोर्स के गठन भेल छल। ई नियमित आकलन स नेपाल दूरसंचार के जारी परिचालन प्रक्रिया मे रुकावट या बाधा पहुंचेबाक संभावना कम अछि।”
